v. bearish|v. bullish| Our predictions on prices last quarter were not too bad: we had Pt trading in a probable range of $780 to $1,020, with a best case high of $1,125. In the event the actual range was $769 to $1,113. Our probable range for palladium was rather wide ($180 to $330), with a lot of upside built in based on the premise that any fresh rumours about a lack of Russian stocks had the potential to trigger a strong rally. That did not come to pass and the metal slipped down to briefly touch our worst case low of $160 before recovering to hit $221.75 last week. Rhodium did not challenge either end of our probable range ($800 to $1,700), remaining capped by steady offers above $1,200 but not subject to the kind of “sell at all costs” liquidation that we saw during the third quarter of last year. For the next three months our expectations of PGM prices are broadly neutral. The platinum price has performed very well from an investment perspective since late October and we think a period of largely sideways trading between $980 and $1,150 is now likely. That said we would not rule out another decent rally from early April onwards as we enter the new financial year for many European and Japanese corporations, and we have pushed our best case high upwards. There is a risk that an upturn in industrial demand will catch the market short of platinum sponge and the sponge–ingot discount could flip to a premium for a while, although that may be more of an issue in Q4 this year. We continue to believe that industrial users who are able to buy platinum one or two years forward would be well advised to consider doing so. We have moved our worst case low price up by $200 to $850. For palladium, both Johnson Matthey and Impala Platinum recently repeated their belief that we are unlikely to see much, if any, palladium sold from Russian state inventories this year. The market, however, is not yet convinced and several tonnes of Russian palladium entered Zurich in January. In light of this we have moderated our bullish view somewhat, narrowing our probable range and trimming our best case high. No change on our rhodium forecast; the market remains pretty quiet on both sides, though with a slight bias to the upside. The risk here for industrial users is that certain funds are known to be looking closely at the metal and should one or more of them start accumulating a physical long position the price could react quite quickly. ||**Spot**|**Worst case**

The platinum price has staged a very decent recovery from the Q4 2008 lows, rising almost 50% in US$ terms since our last quarterly report. However, signs are emerging that the current rally may be coming to a close. Open interest in NYMEX platinum futures contracts are at a multi-year high (green circle) and a reversal of this trend would imply the liquidation of fund long positions. The first significant area of support lies between $990 and $1,010. ## **Mitsubishi Cor oration** **p** Palladium, daily,
last 12 months
Palladium has also climbed away from the Q4 2008 lows but the move has been less convincing than that of platinum. ETF holdings of metal have picked up but net fund positions in NYMEX futures have not changed dramatically over the last three months. Suggestions that Russia may no longer sell significant quantities of metal from state-owned inventories seem premature: 8 tonnes of Russian palladium was shipped to Zurich in January. Palladium also faces stiff chart resistance around the 240 area – it will take substantial and sustained fund buying to push through that barrier. Still, it is worth keeping an eye on the platinum: palladium ratio – the market Platinum:Palladium ratio

v. bearish|v. bullish| Oh dear. No green shoots of recovery in the auto sector yet. Sales and production

have slumped to levels that no-one would have imagined possible 2 years ago. And despite the hefty production cuts and plant closures (both temporary and permanent) inventories of unsold vehicles have continued to climb _(see chart bottom right)_ . But… the fact that in the face of such dismal data, PGM prices have found support and actually moved higher is quite a positive sign for metal producers. In addition, automakers have now run down raw material inventories as far as possible, which suggests that when vehicle sales do start to recover, the effect on metal demand may be magnified as PGM stocks are rebuilt to more normal working levels. That story, however, may have to wait until 2010. USA vehicle sales, year-on-year, %

**5**| |---|---|---|---| |v. bearish|neutral||v. bullish| Purchases of platinum made via the Shanghai Gold Exchange (SGE) have been encouragingly strong over the last three months _(see chart below left)_ . The majority of mainland Chinese jewellery fabricators source a significant proportion of their metal demand from the SGE and the volume traded is a reasonable indicator of the health of the platinum jewellery sector. Trade statistics also show a strong rise in platinum imports to China in 2008, with shipments surging in the final quarter of the year as the local price dropped towards the RMB200/gram mark. However, we remain cautious about the prospects for the remainder of the year for two reasons: 1) stocks of both metal and jewellery were heavily depleted last year as the platinum price soared and companies throughout the sector faced difficulties in funding their inventories. It is likely that the amount of platinum purchased in recent

weeks has been strongly influenced by retailers and wholesalers restocking product lines – if so, this will be a “one-off” boost for platinum demand. 2) With unemployment still rising in the country a degree of concern about retail sales of jewellery and other non-essential goods over the course of the year seems justified. The messages emanating from the major PGM producers are clear, and are clearly bullish for PGM prices over the medium term (see box). One year ago the PGM mining companies in South Africa would have expected to have produced a total of 5.5 million oz of platinum in 2009. Now we forecast production will be less than 4.8 million oz – a drop of 700,000 oz. If current PGM prices and exchange rates persist for another 3 to 6 months we would expect to see additional action to reduce output or suspend production from the least profitable or loss-making shafts. It should be remembered, however, that it takes much less time to cut production than it it will take to increase it again when demand picks up. _“we have slowed down our capital projects to limit our capital expenditure”_ Anglo Platinum _“In the current difficult economic environment cash preservation has become our top priority.”_ Impala Platinum _“the Baobab shaft will be placed on care and maintenance…”_ Lonmin _Aquarius’ people are working through these difficult times, reducing costs and capex…._ Aquarius Platinum _Modikwa: slowing volumes; Two Rivers: mining rate reduced_ African Rainbow Minerals **Mitsubishi Cor oration** **p** ### PGM trade |**-5**

v. bearish| Platinum shipments to Switzerland accelerated sharply in the second half of 2008. Some of this metal represented scrap sold back to dealers during May, June and the first half of July that was subsequently refined and shipped to Zurich (or shipped to Zurich then refined). Then, as the global economy fell off the rails, industrial demand for platinum slumped and the sponge to ingot discount widened to such an extent that refineries began melting excess sponge and delivering the resulting plate into Switzerland. It is interesting to note that US imports of platinum fell by 20 tonnes last year, which was neatly offset by a 13 tonne rise in Chinese imports and a net increase of 7 tonnes in the amount of metal held in Zurich (Swiss imports minus exports). **5**| |---|---|---|---| |v. bearish|neutral||v. bullish| With gold performing so well since the start of the year, it is perhaps not surprising that platinum and palladium have also attracted renewed investment interest. But the PGMs have also been bought on their own merits by individuals (notably in Japan) and institutions who believe that the metals offer good value at current levels and offer the potential of significant gains once the economic outlook improves. There is also a recognition that none of the problems that befell the PGM mining companies last year (strikes, smelter failures, rapid cost inflation, geological problems, safety-related closures, long-term availability of power and water) have been resolved. The upturn in investment buying has been seen across the full range of products, including physical bullion, exchange traded funds, and derivatives (futures and options). However, there is now a sense that after climbing by almost 50% in three months from last October’s low of $744, the platinum price may well be due for a correction lower, particularly if gold also falls back towards $900. The relationship and degree of correlation between the prices of gold and platinum ebb and flow but it’s worth noting that the gold: platinum price ratio rarely drops below 1: 1, and if it does it usually corrects rapidly.
